newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - London market breezes through 4,000 level.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - London market breezes through 4,000 level.

text.p: The psychologically important 4,000-level on the key FTSE index proved little barrier to the London stock market on Wednesday as shares pushed ahead to another all-time high.
The FTSE 100 ended at 4,015.1, up 22.9 points. Advancers beat decliners by a margin of more than two to one.
The benchmark index has rallied some 380 points, or about 10.5 percent, since closing at the year's low of 3,632 on July 16. Today's record close marks the fifth since then.
Yet despite today's surge, the FTSE 100 remains Europe's second worst performing index in Europe after Italy, noted David Aserkoff, a strategist with Credit First Boston.
"The UK market is fairly solid, but I don't see a huge amount of upside," said Aserkoff.
He thinks the FTSE will most likely top out at around 4,050 to 4,100. "I think that's well within reach by year end."

An influx of cash from institutional investors at the start of the fourth quarter on Tuesday and robust performances in bond markets, encouraged by signs of moderate growth and benign inflationary pressures in Britain and America, have created a solid backcloth for the market's rise.
A large trading programme started late on Tuesday and weighted to the buy side, added the final push higher.
Recent rises have been underpinned by hopes of more money coming into the market while the rise has forced institutions with large cash holdings to invest so as not to miss out on further gains.

Fund management group PDFM, with around 15 percent of its holdings in cash is an extreme example, but many other institutions also hold sizeable amounts of cash and hopes this may go into shares continues to bolster sentiment.
"In the very short term, it does appear there's quite a lot of cash sitting on the sidelines waiting to come in," said Panmure Gordon strategist Ian Williams.

"On a week to two week view there's probably more upside to come...over the fourth quarter as a whole we're still a little bit nervous but the underlying liquidity driver is going to be the factor in the near future," he added.

Credit Lyonnais Laing strategist Cory Miller said dividends in coming weeks would be worth as much as three billion pounds ($4.7 billion), and a substantial sum could be reinvested in the rising FTSE 100.

But unease at the current levels of London and New York markets and worries over a reluctance to raise interest rates ahead of elections on both sides of the Atlantic have some warning of sharp corrections ahead.

"We remain cautious looking into next year," said Nomura satrategist Nick Knight, "both as a function of our concerns regarding the U.S. and more particulary with regard to UK monetary policy post the election."
"To a certain extent what's good today may be bad tommorrow for the markets," he added.
Overnight comments from Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan that there were no threats to inflation down the track added to the upbeat mood in London markets from the start.
The market's charge ahead was mirrored on Wall Street overnight where the blue chip Dow Industrials index broke 5,900 for the first time and looks to have 6,000 firmly in its sights.
The Dow was up 24 points when the London markets closed.
The next big hurdle for markets is the closely watched U.S. payroll data due for release on Friday.
